This is the declared command surface. Most command implementations are still
scaffolds; help output does not imply that a command works yet.

## `mammoth`

```text
Distributed storage that doesn't need a JVM

Usage: mammoth [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  init         Create a new cluster: config, IDs, certs
  quickstart   One-command demo cluster with sample data, then open the UI
  serve        Run a node
  ui           Launch or open the web GUI
  doctor       Diagnose config, ports, disks, clock and ulimits
  ls           List a directory
  put          Upload a local file
  get          Download to a local file
  cat          Stream a file to stdout
  tail         Last lines of a file
  head         First lines of a file
  mkdir        Create a directory
  rm           Remove a path
  mv           Move or rename
  cp           Copy within the cluster
  stat         Metadata for one path
  du           Disk usage by path
  df           Cluster capacity summary
  find         Search the namespace
  chmod        Change mode bits
  chown        Change owner or group
  setrep       Change the replication factor
  checksum     Print or verify a file checksum
  viz          Visualize how data is spread across the cluster
  top          Live TUI dashboard — htop for your cluster
  node         Inspect and manage workers
  cluster      Raft membership and leadership
  admin        Cluster administration
  job          Submit and inspect jobs
  migrate      Migrate data in, and upgrade Mammoth itself
  bench        Built-in benchmarks
  config       Inspect and validate configuration
  token        Manage auth tokens
  compat       Translate old Hadoop invocations: `mammoth compat hdfs dfs -ls /`
  completions  Generate a shell completion script
  help         Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -c, --config <CONFIG>
          Path to mammoth.toml

          [env: MAMMOTH_CONFIG=]

      --masters <MASTERS>
          Master addresses, comma separated

          [env: MAMMOTH_MASTERS=]

      --output <OUTPUT>
          Output format

          Possible values:
          - auto:  Table on a terminal, JSON when piped
          - table: Always a human-readable table
          - json:  Always JSON
          - yaml:  Always YAML
          - csv:   Always CSV

          [default: auto]

      --json
          Shorthand for `--output json`. Common enough in scripts to deserve it

  -v, --verbose...
          Repeat for more detail: -v, -vv, -vvv

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

  -V, --version
          Print version
```

## `mammoth viz`

```text
Visualize how data is spread across the cluster

Usage: mammoth viz [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  blocks    Where this file's blocks live, as a block × node matrix
  cluster   Per-node capacity heatmap, grouped by rack
  topology  The rack / zone tree
  skew      Hotspots and partition-size imbalance
  treemap   Which directories are eating the space
  health    Replication health, optionally refreshing live
  flow      Live data movement between clients, replication, balancer and shuffle
  help      Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -c, --config <CONFIG>
          Path to mammoth.toml

          [env: MAMMOTH_CONFIG=]

      --masters <MASTERS>
          Master addresses, comma separated

          [env: MAMMOTH_MASTERS=]

      --output <OUTPUT>

Usage: mammoth viz skew [OPTIONS] [PATH]

Arguments:
  [PATH]
          Directory to analyze

Options:
      --by-partition
          Group by partition directory rather than by file

  -c, --config <CONFIG>
          Path to mammoth.toml

          [env: MAMMOTH_CONFIG=]

      --masters <MASTERS>
          Master addresses, comma separated

          [env: MAMMOTH_MASTERS=]

      --output <OUTPUT>
          Output format

          Possible values:
          - auto:  Table on a terminal, JSON when piped
          - table: Always a human-readable table
          - json:  Always JSON
          - yaml:  Always YAML
          - csv:   Always CSV

          [default: auto]

      --json
          Shorthand for `--output json`. Common enough in scripts to deserve it

  -v, --verbose...
          Repeat for more detail: -v, -vv, -vvv

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```
